title: Partitions, XFS, and mount policy
subtitle: See the whole storage stack, format only what you mean to format, and make a mount survive the next reboot.
objectives: Read the block-device, filesystem, and mount layers
Create and format a partition for XFS
Mount by UUID and persist the mount in /etc/fstab
Add swap and distinguish a swap partition from a swap file

ex200.evidence: Read lsblk, findmnt, df, and blkid output.
Create a partition and format it with mkfs.xfs.

versionNotes: RHEL 9 and RHEL 10 both default to XFS for the root filesystem. XFS can grow online but cannot shrink.
RHEL 10 keeps the same mount and fstab model; newer systems increasingly prefer systemd mount units generated from fstab rather than hand-written unit files.

commands.desc: Create a GPT partition table and one full-disk partition.

lab.title: A file-backed XFS practice disk
lab.scenario: Build capacity from a file, mount it, verify it, and clean up. In production the same operations apply to /dev/sdb1.

steps.text: Inspect the current block devices, filesystems, and mount points.
steps.verify: You can identify the device behind /, /boot, and /data, and their filesystem types.

steps.text: Create a 64 MB file-backed disk and format it as XFS.
steps.cmd: sudo dd if=/dev/zero of=/tmp/lab-disk.img bs=1M count=64 status=progress && sudo mkfs.xfs /tmp/lab-disk.img
steps.verify: mkfs.xfs prints filesystem geometry without refusing the existing data file.

steps.text: Mount it on a new directory and confirm the effective mount.
steps.cmd: sudo mkdir -p /mnt/labdisk && sudo mount -o loop /tmp/lab-disk.img /mnt/labdisk && findmnt /mnt/labdisk
steps.verify: findmnt reports a loop source, the XFS type, and /mnt/labdisk as the target.

steps.text: Write data and check capacity from both filesystem and directory views.
steps.cmd: sudo dd if=/dev/zero of=/mnt/labdisk/fill bs=1M count=20 && df -h /mnt/labdisk && du -sh /mnt/labdisk
steps.verify: df shows used blocks and du accounts for the fill file.

steps.text: Unmount, verify it is gone, and remove the practice image.
steps.cmd: sudo umount /mnt/labdisk && findmnt /mnt/labdisk; sudo rm /tmp/lab-disk.img && sudo rmdir /mnt/labdisk
steps.verify: findmnt returns no row for /mnt/labdisk and the image no longer exists.

quiz.q: Why is a UUID preferred over /dev/sdb1 in /etc/fstab?
options: Device names can move between boots and hardware changes
quiz.why: UUIDs identify the filesystem itself rather than its current enumeration order.

quiz.q: Which command validates fstab entries without rebooting?
quiz.why: mount -a attempts every fstab entry and reports failures while the system is still reachable.

quiz.q: What happens when you run mkfs.xfs on a device that already has an XFS signature?
options: It converts the filesystem to ext4
quiz.why: mkfs.xfs protects existing data. Overwriting requires the explicit -f flag.
